q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Idle time arising from normal causes inherent in workshop working, such as waiting for work or for material in the ordinary course, is treated as a production overhead.
2. Idle time arising from abnormal causes, such as a prolonged general power breakdown or a strike, is kept distinct and is not loaded on the cost of jobs in the ordinary manner.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: normal idle time inherent in workshop working, such as waiting for work or material, is a production overhead, while abnormal idle time from strike or prolonged breakdown is kept distinct and not loaded on jobs ordinarily.

q: The idle time recorded for a worker in a shop is required to be supported by an idle time card or statement mainly so that:

options.A: The causes of idleness can be analysed and responsibility fixed, and the wages for the idle period can be dealt with correctly in costing
options.B: The worker can be fined for every hour of idleness
options.C: The stores depot can price the material issued to the shop
options.D: The outturn of the shop can be transferred to Stores

e: An idle time card or statement supports the recorded idleness so its causes can be analysed, responsibility fixed and the wages for the idle period dealt with correctly in costing.

q: Where overtime is worked in a workshop, the overtime hours of a worker are distinguished in the time booking from his normal hours primarily because:

options.A: Overtime hours are not recorded on the gate cards at all
options.B: The wages for the overtime hours are never paid to the worker
options.C: The extra payment for overtime has to be computed and its incidence in costing — on the job or on on-cost — has to be decided
options.D: Overtime work is always executed under a separate work order

e: Overtime hours are distinguished from normal hours so that the extra overtime payment can be computed and its costing incidence - on the job or on on-cost - correctly decided.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Overtime worked on a job at the specific requirement of the indentor to expedite that job is treated as part of the cost of that job.
2. General overtime worked to clear the ordinary arrears of a shop, not identifiable with any particular job, is treated as an overhead charge.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: overtime worked at the indentor's specific requirement to expedite a job is charged to that job, while general overtime to clear shop arrears is an overhead charge.

q: Under a piece-work (payment by results) arrangement in a shop, control over the labour cost of a job differs from that under day-work (time rate) in that under piece-work:

options.A: No record of the output produced is necessary for costing
options.B: Labour cost is charged wholly to on-cost in both systems
options.C: Time booking of workers on jobs becomes more important than output recording
options.D: The labour cost is linked directly to the quantity of accepted output, whereas under day-work the cost can be controlled only through strict booking of the time spent on each job

e: Under piece-work, labour cost is linked directly to the quantity of accepted output, while under day-work cost can be controlled only through strict booking of time spent on each job.

q: Day-work (time-rate) payment in a workshop places greater reliance on time booking for costing because:

options.A: Wages under day-work are not paid at all unless a job is completed
options.B: Output under day-work is automatically measured by the pay sheet
options.C: Piece rates for every job are fixed under day-work
options.D: The wages paid for attendance have no direct relation to output, so the cost of a job can be known only by distributing the time wages over the jobs on which time was booked

e: Under day-work, wages are paid for attendance and bear no direct relation to output, so job cost is known only by distributing the time wages over jobs from the time booked on each.

q: In batch manufacture of standard components in a workshop, the machine setting-up cost incurred for a batch is treated in costing by:

options.A: Spreading it over all the articles produced in the batch, so that the setting-up cost per article falls as the size of the batch increases
options.B: Charging it wholly to the first article produced in the batch
options.C: Charging it to general on-cost of the workshop in all cases
options.D: Recovering it from the workers engaged on the batch

e: Machine setting-up cost for a batch is spread over all articles produced in the batch, so the setting-up cost per article falls as the size of the batch increases.

q: A batch cost sheet in a workshop differs from a job cost sheet in that the batch cost sheet shows:

options.A: The cost of one single article ordered by a customer
options.B: Only the material cost of the batch, labour and on-cost being excluded
options.C: The total cost of the whole lot produced under the batch order, from which the cost per article of the lot is derived
options.D: The wages of the shop for one day only

e: A batch cost sheet shows the total cost of the whole lot produced under the batch order - labour, material and on-cost - from which the cost per article of the lot is derived.

q: Scrap arising in the course of manufacture on a job, which was allowed for as a normal feature of the manufacturing process in the estimate of the job, is dealt with in costing by:

options.A: Loading its entire value as an extra charge over and above the job cost
options.B: Crediting its realisable value to the job, the net cost of the normal scrap being borne by the good outturn of the job
options.C: Crediting its value to the Pension Fund
options.D: Treating it as a sale by the shop and keeping the proceeds outside the accounts

e: Normal scrap allowed for in the job estimate is credited to the job at its realisable value, so the net cost of that scrap is borne by the good outturn of the job.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Scrap arising on jobs is handed over to the stores depot, which arranges its disposal and accounts for the sale proceeds.
2. The shop executing the job itself sells the scrap arising on the job and retains the sale proceeds towards the cost of the job.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 only is correct: scrap arising on jobs is handed over to the stores depot, which arranges its disposal and accounts for the sale proceeds; the shop does not sell it itself.

q: Under-absorption of on-cost in a workshop for a period means that:

options.A: Jobs done during the period have been charged with more on-cost than was actually incurred
options.B: No on-cost at all was incurred during the period
options.C: Jobs done during the period have borne less on-cost than the on-cost actually incurred, leaving a part of the actual on-cost unrecovered in job costs
options.D: On-cost has been charged to jobs at double the prescribed rate

e: Under-absorption means jobs in the period bore less on-cost than was actually incurred, leaving part of the actual on-cost unrecovered in job costs.

q: Over-absorption of on-cost in a workshop for a period indicates that:

options.A: The jobs done during the period have together been charged with on-cost in excess of the on-cost actually incurred
options.B: The workshop has incurred no indirect expenditure during the period
options.C: The balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense has become nil
options.D: Direct labour booked on jobs exceeds the wages paid

e: Over-absorption means jobs in the period were together charged on-cost in excess of the on-cost actually incurred in the workshop during that period.

q: A persistent under-absorption of shop on-cost in a workshop is most likely to arise when:

options.A: The outturn of the shop increases well beyond the programme
options.B: The outturn of the shop falls well short of the level assumed in fixing the rate, while the largely fixed indirect expenses of the shop continue to be incurred
options.C: Direct wages booked on jobs increase during the period
options.D: Material issued to jobs is returned to the depot as surplus

e: Persistent under-absorption arises when outturn falls well below the level assumed in fixing the rate while the largely fixed indirect expenses of the shop continue to be incurred.

q: The difference between the on-cost absorbed on jobs and the actual on-cost incurred in a workshop is dealt with at the close of the period by:

options.A: Ignoring it permanently, since predetermined rates are used
options.B: Recovering it from the wages of the workers of the shop
options.C: Debiting it to Stores Suspense in all cases
options.D: Adjustment in the workshop accounts — by a supplementary charge or credit to jobs where the difference is material, or by transfer as an on-cost adjustment where it is not taken to individual jobs

e: The difference between absorbed and actual on-cost is adjusted in workshop accounts - by supplementary charge or credit to jobs if material, or as an on-cost adjustment if not taken to individual jobs.

q: In the Workshop General Register, the folio opened for a work order, besides the total debits booked on it, also shows:

options.A: The credits given to the work order on transfer of its outturn and the balance still outstanding against it
options.B: The leave account of the workers engaged on the job
options.C: The price ledger balance of every stores item used on the job
options.D: The programme of the workshop for the following year

e: A work order folio in the Workshop General Register shows, besides total debits booked, the credits given on transfer of outturn and the balance still outstanding against the order.

q: The Workshop General Register serves estimate control over workshop jobs because it enables the Workshop Accounts Office to watch, work order by work order:

options.A: Only the quantity of outturn turned out by each shop
options.B: The sale price of the articles manufactured on the job
options.C: The attendance of the staff engaged on the job
options.D: The expenditure actually booked against the amount of the sanctioned estimate for the job, so that a likely excess is noticed before the job is completed

e: The General Register enables work-order-wise watch of expenditure actually booked against the sanctioned estimate, so a likely excess over estimate is noticed before the job is completed.

q: Monthly reconciliation between the outlay booked on jobs and the outturn transferred out of a workshop is watched mainly to ensure that:

options.A: Every job is completed within one month of its commencement
options.B: The wages of all workers are paid by the end of the month
options.C: No completed outturn remains untransferred and no expenditure remains unexplained, the residue representing only genuine work-in-progress
options.D: The stores depot issues no material in the following month

e: Monthly reconciliation of outlay with outturn ensures no completed outturn remains untransferred and no expenditure remains unexplained, the residue being only genuine work-in-progress.

q: Material drawn from the stores depot for the Periodic Overhaul of rolling stock is distinguished in workshop accounting from material drawn for manufacture of articles for stocking in that:

options.A: POH material is not accounted for through work orders at all
options.B: Both are finally charged to Stores Suspense permanently
options.C: POH material is booked on POH work orders and its cost is finally transferred to the revenue overhaul head, whereas manufacture material is booked on manufacture work orders and its cost is finally transferred to Stores on completion of the articles
options.D: Manufacture material is charged directly to revenue in all cases

e: POH material is booked on POH work orders and finally transferred to the revenue overhaul head, while manufacture material is booked on manufacture orders and finally transferred to Stores.

q: Labour, material and on-cost booked on the Periodic Overhaul of rolling stock belonging to another railway are accumulated on work orders which are kept distinct in the workshop accounts mainly so that:

options.A: The total cost of the overhaul can be recovered from the owning railway and is not merged with the cost of the home railway's own overhaul work
options.B: The workers on the job can be paid at a different rate of wages
options.C: The job can be excluded from the Workshop Outturn Statement
options.D: The material for the job can be drawn without a requisition

e: Overhaul work for another railway is kept on distinct work orders so its total cost can be recovered from the owning railway and not merged with the home railway's own overhaul cost.

q: Mid-Life Rehabilitation of a coach differs from its Periodic Overhaul in that Mid-Life Rehabilitation:

options.A: Is a routine overhaul repeated at every overhaul periodicity of the coach
options.B: Is a heavy, once-in-mid-life renewal involving extensive body and corrosion repairs and renewal of fittings, over and above the scope of a normal Periodic Overhaul
options.C: Consists only of washing and examination of the coach
options.D: Is carried out at the coaching depot and never in a workshop

e: Mid-Life Rehabilitation is a heavy, once-in-mid-life renewal with extensive body and corrosion repairs and renewal of fittings, well beyond the scope of a normal Periodic Overhaul.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Work relating to Mid-Life Rehabilitation of coaches is executed in workshops under work orders through Workshop Manufacturing Suspense, like other workshop work.
2. Mid-Life Rehabilitation work is executed without any work order and its cost is charged directly to shop on-cost.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 only is correct: Mid-Life Rehabilitation is executed in workshops under work orders through WMS like other workshop work, never as a direct charge to shop on-cost.

q: Repairs to rolling stock belonging to a private siding owner, when executed in a railway workshop, are accounted for on the footing that:

options.A: Their cost is borne finally by the Railway as a public service
options.B: Their cost is charged to the Periodic Overhaul programme of the home railway
options.C: Their cost is merged with the cost of the Railway's own stock of the same class
options.D: Their cost, together with the charges leviable, is recoverable from the siding owner, the work being treated as work done for an outside party

e: Repairs to a private siding owner's stock in a railway workshop are work for an outside party, so the cost together with leviable charges is recoverable from the siding owner.

q: A workshop worker deputed for a part of a month on work which is not covered by any measured job or allowed time is, for that part of the month under the incentive arrangements:

options.A: Paid bonus at the highest rate earned in the shop
options.B: Paid no wages at all for that part of the month
options.C: Paid his time-rate (fall-back) wages for the period, without incentive bonus for that period
options.D: Treated as absent without leave for that period

e: For work not covered by any measured job or allowed time, a worker gets only his time-rate fall-back wages for that period, without incentive bonus for that period.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Incentive bonus under a workshop incentive scheme is earned only for the time actually worked on covered work.
2. Bonus is earned by a worker also for the periods of his leave and recorded idle time, at the same rate as for time worked on jobs.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 only is correct: incentive bonus is earned only for time actually worked on covered work; no bonus is earned for leave or recorded idle time.

q: Staff of a workshop whose duties are of a general supervisory or ministerial nature and who are not attached to a shop or group covered by the incentive scheme are, in relation to incentive bonus:

options.A: Paid bonus at the average rate of the whole workshop in all cases
options.B: Outside the incentive scheme and paid no incentive bonus
options.C: Paid bonus at double the rate of direct workers
options.D: Paid bonus only out of the savings in material cost

e: Supervisory and ministerial staff not attached to a shop or group covered by the scheme are outside the incentive scheme and are paid no incentive bonus.

q: The allowed time fixed for an operation of a job is quoted on the operation or job documents of the shop mainly so that:

options.A: The stores depot can work out the issue price of material
options.B: The time actually taken can be compared with it in the shop and the bonus earned on the operation can be computed
options.C: The gate keeper can regulate the entry of the workers
options.D: The completion report of the job can be dispensed with

e: Allowed time is quoted on operation and job documents so the time actually taken can be compared with it in the shop and the bonus earned on the operation can be computed.

q: The periodicity prescribed for the Periodic Overhaul of rolling stock is not one uniform period for all stock, because:

options.A: Each workshop is free to fix its own periodicity for the stock homed to it
options.B: The periodicity is fixed by the stores depot for each class of stock
options.C: Periodicity is prescribed separately for different classes of stock with reference to their type, construction and utilisation in service
options.D: Stock is overhauled only when the Workshop Accounts Officer so directs

e: POH periodicity is prescribed separately for different classes of stock with reference to their type, construction and utilisation in service, so it is not one uniform period for all stock.

q: Before a manufacture job for an outside party on a deposit-work basis is delivered on completion, the workshop accounts ensure that:

options.A: The article is delivered first and its cost is recovered at leisure thereafter
options.B: The full cost of the job, with the charges leviable, stands recovered or adjusted against the deposit made by the party
options.C: The cost of the job is written off to shop on-cost
options.D: The party is granted a discount equal to the on-cost of the job

e: Before delivery of deposit work, the workshop accounts ensure the full cost with leviable charges stands recovered or adjusted against the deposit made by the outside party.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Work done by a workshop for another Government department is billed at cost together with the departmental charges leviable on such work.
2. Work done by a workshop for its own railway is transferred at cost, without the addition of departmental charges as in the case of outside work.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: work for another Government department is billed at cost plus leviable departmental charges, while work for the own railway is transferred at cost without such charges.

q: 'Cannibalisation' of rolling stock components in workshop and depot practice means:

options.A: Manufacturing a new component in place of a worn-out one
options.B: Reconditioning a worn-out component back to its standard size
options.C: Condemning a component and selling it as scrap
options.D: Removing a serviceable component from one unit and fitting it on another unit to keep the latter in service, the donor unit being made good in due course

e: Cannibalisation means removing a serviceable component from one unit and fitting it on another to keep the latter in service, the donor unit being made good in due course.

q: Reclamation of a component in a workshop differs from cannibalisation in that reclamation:

options.A: Consists of removing the component from another unit in service
options.B: Is done only in the stores depot and never in a shop
options.C: Requires no work order or accountal of any kind
options.D: Is the building up and machining of the worn component itself back to a serviceable standard, instead of obtaining the part from another unit

e: Reclamation is building up and machining the worn component itself back to a serviceable standard, unlike cannibalisation which obtains the part from another unit.

q: A sanctioned estimate for a workshop manufacture job, by itself, does not authorise the booking of expenditure on the job, because:

options.A: Expenditure can be booked only against a work order issued for the job, the estimate merely sanctioning the cost of the work
options.B: Estimates for workshop jobs are sanctioned only after the job is completed
options.C: Work orders are issued by the stores depot and not by the workshop
options.D: Booking of expenditure in a workshop requires no authority of any kind

e: A sanctioned estimate only sanctions the cost of the work; expenditure can be booked only against a work order issued for the job, so the estimate alone does not authorise booking.

q: The on-cost standing work orders maintained for collecting the indirect expenses of a shop differ from ordinary job work orders in that the on-cost standing work orders:

options.A: Are transferred out as outturn to Stores on completion
options.B: Represent jobs executed for other railways
options.C: Are cleared not by transfer of any outturn, but by distribution of the amount collected on them over the jobs done in the shop
options.D: Are closed only at the end of ten years

e: On-cost standing work orders collect a shop's indirect expenses and are cleared by distributing the amount collected over the jobs done in the shop, not by transfer of any outturn.

q: Work done by a workshop for another accounting unit is billed to that unit through a transfer certificate or advice, acceptance of which by the receiving unit is necessary mainly so that:

options.A: The debit raised by the workshop is duly taken to account by the receiving unit and does not remain outstanding in the Account Current
options.B: The workers of the workshop can be paid their wages
options.C: The stores depot can close its price ledger for the month
options.D: The outturn programme of the receiving unit is increased

e: Acceptance of the transfer certificate or advice by the receiving unit ensures the debit raised by the workshop is duly taken to account and does not remain outstanding in the Account Current.

q: In workshop costing terminology, a shop of a workshop is treated as a cost centre, while the job or work order executed in it is the:

options.A: Profit centre of the workshop
options.B: Cost unit, for which the cost collected at the cost centre is finally ascertained
options.C: Suspense head of the workshop
options.D: Allocation head of the job

e: A shop is a cost centre where cost is collected, while the job or work order is the cost unit for which the cost collected at that centre is finally ascertained.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The cost of the power house of a workshop, which serves all the shops, is first collected as a service cost centre.
2. That cost is thereafter brought into the cost of jobs by direct charging to each individual job, without reference to the shops served.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 only is correct: the power house serving all shops is first a service cost centre; its cost is then apportioned to the shops served, not charged directly to each individual job.

q: A worker is transferred from one shop of a workshop to another shop in the middle of a month. For incentive and costing purposes, the correct treatment is that:

options.A: His whole month's time and bonus are dealt with in the shop from which he was transferred
options.B: His time is booked and his incentive is computed separately for the period worked in each shop, according to the work done and the scheme applicable there
options.C: He earns no incentive at all for that month
options.D: His wages for the whole month are charged to general on-cost

e: On transfer between shops mid-month, a worker's time is booked and his incentive computed separately for the period in each shop, according to the work done and scheme applicable there.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The time keeper's record establishes the total attendance time for which a workshop worker is to be paid.
2. The shop's job cards and tally sheets establish how that attendance time was spent, job-wise and on idle time.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the time keeper's record establishes total attendance time payable, and job cards and tally sheets establish how that time was spent, job-wise and on idle time.

q: Expenditure on the training of workshop staff in a trade training school attached to the workshop is not charged to individual jobs because:

options.A: Training is imparted only to staff who have retired
options.B: The trainees execute all the manufacture jobs of the workshop
options.C: The expenditure is recovered in full from the trainees as fees
options.D: It is a general charge benefiting the workshop as a whole and is therefore borne as an overhead (on-cost) charge

e: Training of workshop staff benefits the workshop as a whole and cannot be charged to individual jobs, so it is borne as a general overhead or on-cost charge.

q: Where the outturn of a workshop for a period consists largely of repair work whose scope varies from unit to unit, comparison of the unit cost of overhaul between periods is useful mainly as:

options.A: A precise measure which by itself finally settles the efficiency of the workshop
options.B: A basis for fixing the wages of the workshop staff
options.C: A substitute for the job-wise costing of the overhauls
options.D: An indicator calling for investigation where the unit cost varies materially, the variation being examined with reference to the scope and condition of the units overhauled

e: Where repair scope varies from unit to unit, unit cost comparison is only an indicator: a material variation calls for investigation with reference to the scope and condition of units overhauled.

q: An operation card accompanying a job in a workshop differs from a job card in that the operation card:

options.A: Records the attendance of the worker at the workshop gate
options.B: Relates to one specified operation of the job, showing the machine and tools to be used and the allowed time for that operation, while the job card records the time spent by an individual worker
options.C: Shows the total wages payable to all workers of the shop for the month
options.D: Is the authority under which material is purchased for the job

e: An operation card relates to one specified operation, showing the machine, tools and allowed time for it, while a job card records the time spent by an individual worker.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The planning office of a workshop prepares, before work is taken in hand, the route sheets, operation sheets and material schedules for jobs.
2. The progress office follows up jobs while they are under execution, chasing delayed operations and materials so that the programme is maintained.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the planning office prepares route sheets, operation sheets and material schedules before work starts, and the progress office follows up jobs during execution to hold the programme.

q: Stage inspection carried out during the manufacture of an article in a workshop serves mainly to:

options.A: Detect defects at an intermediate stage of manufacture itself, so that further work is not wasted on an article already defective
options.B: Replace the final inspection of the finished article altogether
options.C: Fix the wages of the workers engaged on the article
options.D: Price the material issued for the article

e: Stage inspection detects defects at an intermediate stage of manufacture itself, so that further labour and material are not wasted on an article that is already defective.

q: Before a batch of components is taken up for regular production in a shop, the first piece produced is inspected carefully mainly in order to:

options.A: Close the batch work order after the first piece itself
options.B: Fix the piece rate payable to the operator
options.C: Credit the cost of the batch to the stores depot
options.D: Verify the machine setting, tools and method, so that the whole batch is not produced defectively on a wrong setting

e: First-piece inspection before regular batch production verifies the machine setting, tools and method, so the whole batch is not produced defectively on a wrong setting.

q: A shop reports a job as physically complete, but material drawn for the job and found surplus has not yet been returned to the depot and credited. The correct course for the Workshop Accounts Office is to:

options.A: Close the work order at once, ignoring the pending return
options.B: Transfer the outturn at the material cost alone, leaving labour unadjusted
options.C: Keep the work order open until the surplus material is returned and credited and the final cost is compiled, and only then transfer the outturn and close the order
options.D: Charge the value of the surplus material to shop on-cost and close the order

e: The work order must be kept open until surplus material drawn is returned to the depot and credited and the final cost compiled; only then is the outturn transferred and the order closed.

q: A manufacture job is stopped under competent orders after only a part of the ordered quantity has been produced and accepted. Such a work order is dealt with by:

options.A: Keeping it open indefinitely until the full quantity is ordered again
options.B: Transferring the cost of the completed and accepted portion to its final head and short-closing the work order under competent sanction, the balance being dealt with under orders
options.C: Charging the entire cost booked on it to shop on-cost
options.D: Transferring the cost of the unproduced portion also to Stores as outturn

e: A job stopped after part production is dealt with by transferring the cost of the completed and accepted portion to its final head and short-closing the order under competent sanction.

q: A partly executed job is transferred from one workshop to another workshop for completion. In the accounts of the receiving workshop, the cost already accumulated on the job and received through transfer is:

options.A: Ignored, the receiving workshop costing only the work done by it
options.B: Charged to the shop on-cost of the receiving workshop
options.C: Recovered from the transferring workshop in cash
options.D: Taken as the opening cost of the job under the work order opened by it, further cost being added thereon so that the total cost of the job remains complete

e: Cost already accumulated and received through transfer is taken as the opening cost of the job in the receiving workshop, and further cost is added to it so total job cost remains complete.

q: The capacity utilisation of a repair workshop for a period is judged mainly by comparing:

options.A: The units actually overhauled and turned out during the period with the overhaul capacity available in the workshop for that period
options.B: The wages paid in the period with the wages paid in the previous period
options.C: The material consumed in the period with the stock held in the depot
options.D: The number of work orders opened with the number of shops in the workshop

e: Capacity utilisation of a repair workshop is judged by comparing units actually overhauled and turned out in the period with the overhaul capacity available for that period.

q: At a periodical budget review, the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense estimates of a workshop are revised mainly with reference to:

options.A: The cash balance available in the workshop imprest
options.B: The figures of the previous year repeated without change
options.C: The trend of actual outlay and outturn during the year and the revised programme of manufacture and overhaul work for the remaining period
options.D: The number of staff retiring during the remaining period

e: At budget review, WMS estimates are revised with reference to the trend of actual outlay and outturn during the year and the revised programme for the remaining period.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The share of the value of time saved paid to the worker as bonus is smaller under the Halsey-Weir plan than under the Halsey plan.
2. Under the Halsey-Weir plan, the worker receives the entire value of the time saved by him as bonus.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 only is correct: Halsey plan pays 50 per cent of time saved and Halsey-Weir pays a smaller share, 30 per cent; the worker does not get the entire value under Halsey-Weir.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the CLW pattern scheme, the bonus of a worker rests on the time saved by him individually against the allowed time for the work done by him.
2. Under the Group Incentive Scheme, the bonus of the group rests on the accepted outturn of the group measured against its target, expressed in standard hours.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: under the CLW pattern, bonus rests on time saved individually against allowed time, and under the group scheme, bonus rests on the group's accepted outturn in standard hours against target.

q: A gang turns out accepted work whose total allowed time is more than the time actually spent by the gang on that work, excluding recorded idle time and leave. In incentive terms, the excess of the allowed time over the time so spent represents:

options.A: Overtime worked by the gang
options.B: The time saved on the work, on the basis of which the incentive bonus of the gang is worked out
options.C: Unaccounted time to be charged to shop on-cost
options.D: The time to be carried forward as allowed time for the next job

e: Allowed time in excess of time actually spent by the gang, excluding idle time and leave, is the time saved on the work, on which the gang's incentive bonus is worked out.

q: In motion study, a SIMO (simultaneous motion cycle) chart is used to record:

options.A: The movement of material between the shops of a workshop
options.B: The programmed and actual outturn of a shop side by side
options.C: The breakdowns suffered by the machines of a shop
options.D: The simultaneous movements of the two hands of a worker, element by element, in a short-cycle operation

e: A SIMO chart in motion study records the simultaneous movements of the two hands of a worker, element by element, in a short-cycle operation, to analyse and improve the method.

q: A multiple activity (man-machine) chart prepared in work study shows, side by side:

options.A: The working time and idle time of the worker and of the machine during a cycle, so that idle time of either can be reduced
options.B: The material issued and the material returned on a job
options.C: The allowed times of successive jobs done in the shop
options.D: The wages earned by the worker on successive days

e: A multiple activity or man-machine chart shows side by side the working and idle time of the worker and of the machine during a cycle, so idle time of either can be reduced.

q: In workshop costing, the conversion cost of a job means:

options.A: The direct material cost of the job alone
options.B: The direct labour cost and the on-cost charged on the job, that is, the cost of converting the material into the finished article, excluding the material cost itself
options.C: The full cost of the job including proforma on-cost
options.D: The departmental charges leviable on the job

e: Conversion cost is direct labour plus on-cost charged on the job - the cost of converting material into the finished article - excluding the direct material cost itself.

q: Operation costing, as applied to workshop production, is best described as:

options.A: Costing of a single specific order from start to finish in one shop only
options.B: Pure process costing applied to a continuous chemical process
options.C: A hybrid method in which cost is collected operation by operation, suited to repetitive production passing through standard operations
options.D: Marginal costing applied to repair jobs only

e: Operation costing is a hybrid method in which cost is collected operation by operation, suited to repetitive production passing through a series of standard operations.

q: Cost reduction in a workshop differs from cost control in that cost reduction aims at:

options.A: Merely keeping the actual cost within the standard or estimate for the existing method of working
options.B: Preparing the cost sheets of jobs promptly every month
options.C: Comparing the unit costs of two workshops with each other
options.D: A permanent lowering of the cost per unit by improving methods, design or processes, without impairing the quality or usefulness of the outturn

e: Cost reduction aims at a permanent lowering of cost per unit by improving methods, design or processes without impairing quality or usefulness, unlike cost control which only holds cost within standard.

q: Value analysis applied to a component manufactured in a workshop is directed mainly to:

options.A: Examining the function performed by the component and finding a cheaper material, design or method that performs the same function equally well
options.B: Raising the price at which the component is transferred to Stores
options.C: Reducing the wages of the workers producing the component
options.D: Dispensing with the inspection of the component

e: Value analysis examines the function performed by a component and seeks a cheaper material, design or method that performs the same function equally well.

q: Nuts, bolts and washers of trifling value are issued in bulk to a shop and are not booked job-wise, although they are used on identifiable jobs. This treatment rests on the costing practice that:

options.A: Such material is a free gift of the stores depot
options.B: Material of very small value is treated as a consumable charge to on-cost for convenience, the cost and effort of booking it to each job being out of proportion to its value
options.C: Such material is charged to the first job of the month in full
options.D: Such material is recovered from the workers using it

e: Material of very small value, like nuts, bolts and washers, is treated as a consumable on-cost charge for convenience, as job-wise booking would cost more in effort than the material is worth.

q: The amount to be quoted or demanded in advance for manufacture work undertaken for an outside party is worked out on the basis of:

options.A: The prime cost of the work alone
options.B: The direct material cost of the work alone
options.C: The estimated full cost of the work, including on-cost and proforma charges, together with the departmental charges leviable on such work
options.D: The market price of a similar article, without reference to the cost of the work

e: The advance demand for outside work is based on the estimated full cost including on-cost and proforma charges, together with the departmental charges leviable on such work.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. On-cost rates are fixed with reference to the normal capacity working of the workshop, so that the cost of jobs is not distorted by purely temporary fluctuations in the volume of outturn.
2. On-cost rates are fixed afresh every month strictly on the actual hours worked in that month alone.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 only is correct: on-cost rates are fixed with reference to normal capacity working so temporary fluctuations in outturn do not distort job costs; they are not refixed monthly on actual hours alone.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The cost of repairing the machinery of a shop is finally borne as part of the on-cost of the shop owning the machinery.
2. The cost of Periodic Overhaul of rolling stock is finally transferred to the revenue overhaul head of the railway owning the stock.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: repair cost of a shop's machinery is finally borne in that shop's on-cost, and POH cost of rolling stock is finally transferred to the revenue overhaul head of the owning railway.

q: Work is completed in a workshop for another railway and its cost is to be recovered from that railway. The amount billed against the other railway is:

options.A: The direct material cost of the work alone
options.B: A lump sum fixed by the shop incharge
options.C: The full cost of the work including proforma on-cost, recovered through transfer transactions between the two railways
options.D: The wages of the workers engaged on the work alone

e: Work done for another railway is billed at full cost including proforma on-cost, and the amount is recovered through transfer transactions between the two railways.

q: Articles produced on a job are rejected on final inspection as not conforming to specification. Until they are rectified and accepted, or otherwise disposed of under orders, the articles are:

options.A: Transferred to the stores depot as good stock at full cost
options.B: Not transferred out as outturn, their cost remaining under the job in Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.C: Sold by the shop as scrap without any record
options.D: Written off to general on-cost without any orders

e: Articles rejected on final inspection are not transferred out as outturn; their cost remains on the job under WMS until they are rectified and accepted or otherwise disposed of under orders.

q: Under payment by results in a shop, the quantity for which a worker is paid is taken from:

options.A: The piece-work tickets showing the quantity produced by him and passed as accepted after inspection
options.B: The gate attendance cards of the worker
options.C: The material requisitions issued to the shop
options.D: The completion report of the last job of the shop

e: Under payment by results, the quantity paid for is taken from piece-work tickets showing the quantity produced by the worker and passed as accepted after inspection.

q: A machine utilisation statement maintained in a workshop brings out, machine-wise or shop-wise:

options.A: The wages paid to the operators of each machine
options.B: The quantity of material consumed on each machine
options.C: The hours for which the machines were available, the hours actually worked and the hours lost with reasons such as breakdown or want of work
options.D: The scrap produced on each machine during the month

e: A machine utilisation statement shows, machine-wise or shop-wise, hours available, hours actually worked and hours lost with reasons such as breakdown or want of work.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Idle facilities in a workshop mean the time for which individual workers remain waiting for work or material.
2. Idle facilities mean the plant and machine capacity of the workshop lying unused, although the standing charges on that capacity continue to be incurred.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 2 only is correct: idle facilities mean plant and machine capacity lying unused while standing charges continue; workers waiting for work is idle time, not idle facilities.

q: At a periodical check of tools issued on loan to workers, a tool recorded against a worker is found missing. The matter is dealt with by:

options.A: Ignoring the shortage, tools being consumable in nature
options.B: Charging the value of all tools of the shop to shop on-cost
options.C: Closing the tool loan account of the whole shop
options.D: Investigating the shortage and, where the worker is responsible, recovering the value of the missing tool from him under orders, the loan account being adjusted accordingly

e: A missing loan tool is investigated and, where the worker is responsible, its value is recovered from him under orders, the tool loan account being adjusted accordingly.

q: Master or reference gauges kept in the standards or gauge room of a workshop are used for:

options.A: Checking and calibrating the working gauges and measuring instruments used in the shops, so that accuracy of measurement is preserved throughout the workshop
options.B: Measuring the output of every job produced in the shops
options.C: Marking out work on castings in the foundry
options.D: Checking the attendance of workers at the gate

e: Master or reference gauges in the gauge room are used for checking and calibrating the working gauges and measuring instruments used in the shops, preserving accuracy of measurement.

q: In foundry working, an unfavourable yield variance for a period points mainly to:

options.A: An increase in the wages of foundry workers
options.B: A fall in the price of pig iron purchased
options.C: A lower proportion of good castings obtained from the metal melted than the standard yield, indicating higher melting loss or rejection in the foundry
options.D: An increase in the number of moulds prepared in the foundry

e: An unfavourable foundry yield variance means a lower proportion of good castings was obtained from the metal melted than the standard yield, indicating higher melting loss or rejection.

q: The net cost borne by a workshop on running a subsidised canteen for its staff is treated in workshop costing as:

options.A: A direct charge on the jobs under execution in the shops
options.B: A welfare overhead borne as general on-cost of the workshop
options.C: Proforma on-cost of the workshop
options.D: A recovery from the wages of the staff using the canteen

e: The net cost of a subsidised staff canteen is a welfare expense benefiting the workshop as a whole, so it is borne as general on-cost, not charged to individual jobs.

q: Line balancing in a production line of a workshop consists of:

options.A: Drawing a line on the shop floor along which components are queued
options.B: Fixing the wages of all workers of the line at one uniform rate
options.C: Loading every machine of the line with the same number of jobs, irrespective of the time taken
options.D: Distributing the work among the successive stations of the line so that each station takes about the same time, avoiding bottlenecks at some stations and idleness at others

e: Line balancing distributes work among successive stations of a production line so each station takes about the same time, avoiding bottlenecks at some stations and idleness at others.

q: Sequencing of jobs on a machine or in a shop, as a production control function, means:

options.A: Deciding the order in which the waiting jobs will be taken up on the machine, so that machine time is used to the best advantage and urgent jobs are not held up
options.B: Deciding the shops through which a job will pass during manufacture
options.C: Fixing the dates by which the annual programme is to be completed
options.D: Inspecting the jobs in the order of their completion

e: Sequencing means deciding the order in which waiting jobs will be taken up on a machine or in a shop, so machine time is used to best advantage and urgent jobs are not held up.

q: During the Periodic Overhaul of a coach, dismantling reveals heavy corrosion repairs which were not foreseen when the overhaul was taken in hand. The correct course is to:

options.A: Execute the extra repairs and book them without any further authority
options.B: Abandon the overhaul of the coach altogether
options.C: Get the additional work approved and the estimate for the job revised or supplemented, and book the extra cost against the work order under that authority
options.D: Book the extra cost to shop on-cost so that the overhaul cost is not increased

e: Extra corrosion repairs found on dismantling during POH need approval and revision or supplementation of the job estimate, and the extra cost is booked to the work order under that authority.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A completion report relates to one job and is rendered when that job is completed.
2. The Workshop Outturn Statement is a periodical compilation for the shops as a whole, covering all the jobs completed and the expenditure booked during the period.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: a completion report relates to one job on its completion, while the Workshop Outturn Statement is a periodical compilation for the shops as a whole for the period.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A transfer certificate rendered by a workshop is the periodical compilation of all transfer transactions of the workshop for a month.
2. The Account Current of a workshop is a single advice covering one individual transaction with another accounting unit.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Neither is correct: a transfer certificate covers one individual transaction with another unit, while the Account Current is the periodical compilation of transfer transactions - the statements reverse the two.

q: Components from several shops of a workshop are sent to the heat treatment shop for hardening and tempering. The working expenses of the heat treatment shop are brought into job costs by:

options.A: Charging them directly to the first job received in the month
options.B: Debiting them to Stores Suspense
options.C: Recovering them from the workers of the shops served
options.D: Apportioning them among the shops served, as part of the on-cost burden of those shops

e: Working expenses of the heat treatment shop, a service shop, are apportioned among the shops it serves as part of their on-cost burden, and so reach the job costs of those shops.

q: A shop in which the work is predominantly done on machines will absorb its on-cost on jobs most suitably on the basis of:

options.A: Direct labour hours worked on the jobs
options.B: Machine hours worked on the jobs
options.C: The floor area occupied by each job
options.D: The number of workers attending the shop

e: In a predominantly machine-based shop, on-cost is most suitably absorbed on machine hours worked on jobs, as the indirect expenses relate mainly to machine working.

q: A deposit work is completed and its final cost, with charges, is found to be less than the amount deposited by the party in advance. The balance remaining is dealt with by:

options.A: Crediting it to shop on-cost of the workshop
options.B: Retaining it permanently under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.C: Adjusting the final cost against the deposit and refunding the unspent balance to the party, any shortfall being recovered before delivery
options.D: Treating it as earnings of the workshop

e: On completion of deposit work, the final cost with charges is adjusted against the deposit, the unspent balance is refunded to the party, and any shortfall is recovered before delivery.

q: A stores depot requires replenishment of its stock of a standard component manufactured in the workshop. The manufacture is taken in hand:

options.A: Against an indent placed by the stores depot on the workshop, a manufacture work order being issued for the quantity indented
options.B: On a verbal request of the depot storekeeper, without any work order
options.C: By charging the cost directly to the depot stock account, without passing through the workshop accounts
options.D: Only after the stock of the component in the depot has become nil and traffic has been held up

e: Replenishment manufacture for a stores depot is taken in hand against an indent placed by the depot on the workshop, with a manufacture work order issued for the quantity indented.

q: The arisings of stock due for Periodic Overhaul in a period exceed the overhaul capacity of the workshop homing that stock. The position is dealt with in programme planning by:

options.A: Overhauling all the arisings regardless of capacity, by booking the excess cost to on-cost
options.B: Condemning the excess stock without any examination
options.C: Charging the excess stock to another workshop without any transfer arrangement
options.D: Carrying the excess forward as a backlog of overdue overhauls, the programme being arranged with reference to the capacity available and the condition and due dates of the stock

e: Arisings in excess of overhaul capacity are carried forward as a backlog of overdue overhauls, the programme being arranged with reference to available capacity and the condition and due dates of stock.

q: An overhead volume variance in workshop costing arises when:

options.A: The actual indirect expenditure differs from the budgeted indirect expenditure for the period
options.B: The on-cost absorbed on jobs differs from the amount expected because the volume of outturn differs from the budgeted or normal volume on which the absorption rate was based
options.C: The wages rate paid differs from the standard wages rate
options.D: The price of material differs from the standard price of material

e: An overhead volume variance arises when on-cost absorbed differs from the expected amount because the volume of outturn differs from the budgeted or normal volume on which the absorption rate was based.

q: The progress office of a workshop reports jobs which are falling behind the production programme mainly so that:

options.A: The workers on those jobs can be fined for the delay
options.B: The priorities and schedules can be revised by the production control organisation and the delayed jobs expedited
options.C: The work orders of those jobs can be closed at once
options.D: The material for those jobs can be returned to the depot

e: The progress office reports jobs falling behind programme so that priorities and schedules can be revised by production control and the delayed jobs expedited.

q: Components are manufactured in a workshop against the indent of an open-line depot of the same railway for its direct use, and not for stocking in the stores depot. On completion, the cost of the components is:

options.A: Debited to the indenting depot or department through transfer, the articles being delivered directly to it
options.B: Retained permanently under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.C: Credited to the Pension Fund of the railway
options.D: Borne as shop on-cost of the manufacturing shop

e: Components made for direct use of an open-line depot, not for stocking, are on completion debited to the indenting depot or department through transfer and delivered directly to it.

q: Units turned out by a group under the Group Incentive Scheme are rejected on inspection and are not accepted as outturn. For incentive purposes, such rejected units:

options.A: Earn standard hours for the group in the same way as accepted units
options.B: Earn standard hours at double the normal rate, to cover the cost of rectification
options.C: Are counted in the outturn of the following period automatically
options.D: Earn no standard hours and no bonus credit, bonus being worked out only on the accepted outturn

e: Rejected units earn no standard hours and no bonus credit under the Group Incentive Scheme, because bonus is worked out only on the accepted outturn of the group.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Workshop Accounts Officer:
1. He is responsible for the compilation of job costs and the rendering of the workshop accounts.
2. He exercises internal check over the workshop's labour pay sheets, stores transactions and bills.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the Workshop Accounts Officer is responsible for compilation of job costs and rendering of workshop accounts, and exercises internal check over labour pay sheets, stores transactions and bills.

q: The superintendent or incharge of an individual shop contributes to workshop cost control mainly by:

options.A: Rendering the monthly accounts of the workshop to headquarters
options.B: Watching the deployment of labour in his shop, keeping idle time low and controlling the indirect expenses of his shop
options.C: Fixing the on-cost percentages for the workshop as a whole
options.D: Sanctioning the estimates of manufacture jobs

e: A shop superintendent contributes to cost control by watching deployment of labour in his shop, keeping idle time low and controlling the indirect expenses of his shop.

q: The overall responsibility for the efficient working of a railway workshop and for achieving its outturn programme rests with:

options.A: The Workshop Accounts Officer
options.B: The Controller of Stores
options.C: The shop superintendent of the largest shop
options.D: The Chief Workshop Manager

e: Overall responsibility for the efficient working of a railway workshop and for achieving its outturn programme rests with the Chief Workshop Manager.

q: A POH job is held up because a casting has not moved from the foundry for several days. A member of the production control organisation personally chases the foundry and the depot, arranges the movement of the casting and reports the job back on schedule. This function is known as:

options.A: Expediting or follow-up of the job
options.B: Rate fixing
options.C: Job evaluation
options.D: Post-costing

e: Personally chasing a delayed job through the foundry and depot, arranging movement of the casting and bringing the job back on schedule, is the expediting or follow-up function of production control.

q: The route card, material and drawings of a scheduled job are ready, and the production control organisation releases the job to the first shop for work to begin in the planned sequence. This act of putting the schedule into operation at the shop floor is an instance of:

options.A: Inspection
options.B: Dispatching
options.C: Stock verification
options.D: Absorption of on-cost

e: Releasing a scheduled job, with its route card, material and drawings ready, to the first shop for work to begin in the planned sequence is dispatching - putting the schedule into operation.

q: Before deciding whether a component should be manufactured in the railway workshop or purchased from the trade, the comparison that is principally made is between:

options.A: The scrap value of the component and its book value
options.B: The wages of the shop staff and the wages of the supplier's staff
options.C: The estimated workshop cost of manufacture, including on-cost, and the price at which the component can be bought, keeping in view the capacity available in the workshop
options.D: The original cost of the component and its present market price alone

e: The make-or-buy comparison is principally between the estimated workshop cost of manufacture including on-cost and the trade price of the component, keeping in view the capacity available in the workshop.

q: When a workshop is asked to quote a price for work proposed to be done for an outside party, the quotation is built up in advance by:

options.A: Estimated costing, working out the expected material, labour and on-cost charges of the job before it is undertaken
options.B: Waiting till the job is completed and then guessing its cost
options.C: Copying the price charged by a private workshop without any costing
options.D: Charging only the material cost expected on the job

e: A quotation for outside work is built up in advance by estimated costing - working out the expected material, labour and on-cost charges of the job before it is undertaken.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The annual production or POH programme of a workshop is broken down into monthly shop programmes so that work can be loaded evenly.
2. Monthly programmes take into account the capacity of the shops and the stock or orders expected to become available.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the annual production or POH programme is broken into monthly shop programmes for even loading, and monthly programmes take into account shop capacity and stock or orders expected.

q: Material required for the Periodic Overhaul programme of a workshop is planned so that the required items become available in step with the programme of stock coming in for overhaul. This advance phasing of material against the overhaul programme is called:

options.A: Material scheduling
options.B: Cannibalisation
options.C: Stock adjustment
options.D: Reclamation

e: Advance phasing of material so required items become available in step with the programme of stock coming in for Periodic Overhaul is called material scheduling.

q: Before a coach is taken in hand for Periodic Overhaul, the complete set of material required for its overhaul is collected together and kept ready for issue to the job as one set. This practice is known as:

options.A: Kitting of POH material
options.B: Batching of outturn
options.C: Pooling of stores
options.D: Loading of machines

e: Collecting the complete set of material required for a coach's Periodic Overhaul together in advance, ready for issue to the job as one set, is known as kitting of POH material.

q: A bar issued to a job is cut to the sizes required and a usable length remains with the shop after the job is done. The correct treatment of the remaining length is to:

options.A: Retain it in the shop indefinitely without any record
options.B: Treat it as scrap in all cases
options.C: Return it to the stores depot as cut material, so that the job gets credit and the material remains accounted for
options.D: Charge its full value again to the next job

e: A usable length of bar remaining after a job is returned to the stores depot as cut material, so the job gets credit for it and the material remains properly accounted for.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Material drawn for a job but found surplus on its completion should be returned promptly to the depot and the work order credited.
2. The clearance of such surplus material is watched by the accounts office so that completed work orders do not continue to carry the cost of material no longer required.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Both are correct: material drawn for a job but found surplus on completion is returned promptly to the depot with credit to the work order, and accounts watches its clearance so completed orders carry no unwanted cost.

q: A component under manufacture passes from the machine shop to the fitting shop of the same workshop for the next operation. In the workshop accounts, this movement between shops:

options.A: Creates outturn of the machine shop and a fresh work order in the fitting shop
options.B: Is a sale from one shop to the other
options.C: Closes the work order in the machine shop
options.D: Does not create outturn; the cost of both shops continues to accumulate on the same work order till the job is completed

e: Movement of a component between shops of the same workshop creates no outturn and no fresh work order; cost of both shops continues to accumulate on the same work order till the job is completed.

q: Assessment of the remaining useful life of major components, made with reference to their service record and condition, is carried out in a workshop mainly to decide:

options.A: Whether the component should be repaired and refitted, or replaced, at overhaul
options.B: The wages payable to the staff who fitted the component
options.C: The scrap price of the component in an auction
options.D: The periodicity of the incentive bonus

e: Assessment of remaining useful life of major components, from service record and condition, is made mainly to decide whether the component should be repaired and refitted or replaced at overhaul.

q: Serviceable components released from rolling stock under dismantling are dealt with in the workshop by:

options.A: Mixing them with scrap and selling the whole lot together
options.B: Segregating and inspecting them and accounting for them separately as released material, distinct from scrap
options.C: Destroying them so that they are not used again
options.D: Crediting their value to shop on-cost without inspection

e: Serviceable components released from dismantled rolling stock are segregated, inspected and accounted for separately as released material, distinct from scrap, for further use or disposal.
